title: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say

reading.body:
This is a case of an automated alert being treated as an identification. License plate cameras flagged a stolen Camaro in the area, and deputies then stopped a car that matched but whose plates they could not read. The failure sits at the handoff between the camera system and the stop itself, at the moment a partial match was acted on as though it were a confirmed one. Everything that followed, the drawn guns, the handcuffs, the helicopter, rested on that unverified link.

The check that would have caught it is the one the system exists to provide, a confirmed plate read. An unreadable plate is a reason to hold the stop rather than escalate it, and the facts show the stop proceeded without that confirmation. Supervisors will now review body camera video to determine whether procedures were followed, which is a review of the response rather than of the camera match.

What is not established is fault. The account comes from the two men through a single outlet, the deputies' account is not given, and the internal review has not produced a finding. The men were told how to file complaints and both plan to do so, and Anthony's mother plans to hire an attorney, which is not a filed claim and not a determination of anything.

reports.title: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say

summary:
Harris County sheriff's deputies in Cypress, Texas, mistook two 19-year-old men, Anthony and Julian, for car thieves on Aug. 3. Deputies surrounded their Camaro, pointed guns, handcuffed them, and a helicopter circled overhead. Julian said a deputy pushed him down and threatened to shoot him. The men were released after deputies realized it was the wrong car. The stolen Camaro had been linked to aggravated robberies, and license plate cameras had flagged it in the area.

Deputies had spotted a matching car but could not read its plates, so they called backup. After the mistake, supervisors including the district captain, shift lieutenants, and shift sergeants will review body camera video to check whether procedures were followed. The men were told how to file a formal complaint with internal affairs, and both plan to do so. Anthony's mother wants accountability and plans to hire an attorney.
title_en: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say
